b1-001.reason: Answer (reply 3, 8) is only Darwin's farewell and signature to Gray's valediction (para 4); no content.

b1-002.reason: Reply 2 answers Sedgwick's complaint about the concluding chapter's confident tone and appeal to young men (para 5).

b1-003.reason: Reply 1 on Leschenaultia pollen tubes and the stigmatic surface takes up Hooker's para 1 on Goodenia flowers and the viscid surface.

b1-004.reason: Reply 2 is mostly about the American edition (paras 1-3), but it also asks Gray to fix 'self-fertilise itself', which comes from para 7, a separate topic.

b1-005.reason: Reply 1 thanks Sclater for his list of Galapagos birds, which is the whole of the question (paras 1-7, 9).

b1-006.reason: Reply 2 names Wollaston as the Annals reviewer and repeats the Bishop of Oxford's 'unphilosophical' remark, which answers paras 4-5.

b1-007.reason: Reply 3 thanks Galton for the 'other notes' he mentions in the question and comments on sexual selection, which those notes prompted.

b1-008.reason: Reply 6 welcomes the criticisms Gray says he will send later about gaps in the evidence (para 4).

b1-009.reason: Reply 4 says Waterhouse wants to see the worker-to-drone cell gradation, which answers Smith's offer of his comb piece in para 1.

b1-010.reason: Reply 5 asks Gray to thank Wyman for offering hints and regrets Dana's illness, which answers paras 13, 15 and 17.

b1-011.reason: Reply 1 thanks Bunbury for praise (para 1) but also regrets that he is not converted, which answers para 2's 'I am not convinced'.

b1-012.reason: Replies 3, 4 and 6 answer Gray's best and weak points (eye, sterility), his non-committal review and his praise (paras 6-12, 20).

b1-013.reason: Reply 1 answers Hooker's approval of the book in para 1 and the postscript in para 7.

b1-014.reason: Reply 3 comments on Hooker being settled in his Kew house and his heavy workload, which answers para 5.

b1-015.reason: Reply 1 opens with Darwin's own unprompted news of a Madagascar hippopotamus tooth, repeated in reply 2; it never answers the reindeer antler question.

b1-016.reason: Reply 2 identifies the wren (para 8) but also discusses the Zenaida occurring on the mainland, an item that is not in the question.

b1-017.reason: Reply 1 thanks Galton for the pleasure his congratulations on the book gave him (para 1).

b1-018.reason: Reply 4 is only 'Many thanks for your pleasant note' and a signature, matching the valediction in para 7.

b1-019.reason: Reply 6 acknowledges the Asa Gray letter enclosed with para 1 and says he is too sick to read it yet.

b1-020.reason: Reply 1 thanks the booksellers for their French dictionary advice (para 1) and says he will call about it.

b1-022.reason: Reply 3 says whether Darwin can attend the Club and explains his health, which answers Hooker's para 6 about the Club.

b1-024.reason: Reply 3 is closing formula regretting Sedgwick's 'disapprobation and ridicule' (paras 2-4); it ignores his health and heaven remarks (paras 6-7).

b1-025.reason: Reply 1 thanks Spencer and praises his framing of the theory as a hypothesis that explains many facts, which answers paras 1-5.

b1-026.reason: Replies 5 and 6 are only renewed thanks, kind remembrances and a signature, answering Galton's closing regards; no content.

b1-027.reason: Reply 1 admits the Agassiz blunder (para 14) but mainly sends the Historical Preface and corrections, which answers other paragraphs.

b1-028.reason: Reply 1 promises to measure the Jamaican bee cells once Smith makes his final identification, which answers para 1.

b1-030.reason: Reply 1 thanks Gray for his letter to Hooker, and reply 4 also covers Agassiz and H. D. Rogers; only part concerns Wyman's praise (para 3).

b1-032.reason: Replies 2 and 3 cover the American edition, sending new matter, Gray's review and answering Agassiz, which answers paras 1-2.

b1-033.reason: Reply 2 praises Ramsay's general arguments against the immutability of species, set out in paras 1-2.

b1-034.reason: Reply 4 thanks Thwaites for the Lantana report and urges a list of Ceylon's naturalised plants, which answers para 4.

b1-035.reason: Replies 3-5 give Darwin's facts on curved styles and nectaries, including Rhododendron, which answers Hooker's paras 3-4.

b1-036.reason: Replies 1-2 answer Thwaites's objections on beauty, forms not advancing and degeneration (paras 1-3).

b1-038.reason: Reply 5 is only 'With hearty thanks for your letter' and a signature; it ignores the Ceylon invitation (para 5).

b1-039.reason: Reply 7 answers Hooker's remarks that natural selection explains too much (paras 3-5).

b1-040.reason: Reply 2 accepts Galton's correction about the Rhinoceros on p. 68 given in the question.

b1-041.reason: Reply 2 asks to hear more about Owen avowing the Review and compares how Owen treats Hooker and Darwin, which answers para 2.

b1-042.reason: Reply 1 answers the edition and money (paras 1-3); reply 2 adds Darwin's news of Boott, Zoonomia, Owen, converts, Harvey and Macmillan.

b1-044.reason: Replies 2-3 praise Spencer's population pamphlet (para 3) and ask whether to return it.

b1-045.reason: Reply 3 gives Darwin's opinion of Wallace's Linnean paper, answering Lyell's paras 6-7.

b1-046.reason: Replies 2 and 7 answer points on representative species, hybridism and vera causa that are not in para 2, which covers only converts and pièces justificatives.

b1-047.reason: Reply 3 takes up Huxley's second objection in para 7, on why variation occurs if external conditions matter little.

b1-049.reason: Reply 1 answers Sedgwick's disapproval that the book is false and mischievous and his shock (paras 1-4).

b1-050.reason: Reply 6 regrets Lady Hooker's bone inflammation, which answers para 3 on Hooker's bedridden mother.

b1-051.reason: Reply 1 thanks Sclater and discusses Otus and Zenaida, which answers his offer in para 3 to examine those birds.

b1-052.reason: Reply 1 thanks Lyell and discusses Bravard's fossil mammals and Palaeotherium Paranense, which answers paras 2-3.

b1-053.reason: Reply 2 answers Bentham (para 3), but its A. Gray speculation and J. E. Gray's attack are Darwin's own material, not prompted by paras 2-3.

b1-054.reason: Reply 2's 'nunc dimittis' relief at Huxley's verdict answers the whole letter (paras 1-11).

b2-001.reason: Reply para 3's cave-animal diversity argument answers Murray's cave-animal remarks (paras 3, 10); only the closing thanks responds to the reference list in paras 5-9.

b2-002.reason: Reply para 2 rebuts Lyell's para 1 points on Deinosaurian free will and on grouping Huxley's 'matter & force' with natural selection.

b2-003.reason: Reply para 8 answers Lyell's para 8 question on whether the land or marine Amblyrhynchus came first and where it came from.

b2-006.reason: Reply para 7 ('no consolatory view on the dignity of man') directly answers Lyell's paras 1-10 on man's dignity and progressive consolation.

b2-007.reason: Reply para 4 answers Lyell's para 4 question whether Hooker had written about few peculiar Arctic/Greenland forms and his explanation.

b2-009.reason: Reply para 1 formally acknowledges election as Correspondent announced in Stewardson's paras 1-5; para 2 is just the address line.

b2-010.reason: Reply para 2 on hive-bees sucking withered or small clover flowers responds to Hardy's para 2 on smaller second-growth flowers.

b2-011.reason: Reply para 1 reacts to Lyell's news (paras 1-2) that Barrande's primordial/Cambrian is increasingly separated from Lower Silurian.

b2-013.reason: Reply para 1 praises Lyell's remarks as new and says 'I will run through them', referring to objections in paras 3-8 absent from the question.

b2-014.reason: Only 'The facts are really grand' answers Falconer's Sicilian cave news (paras 2-5); most of reply para 1 is Darwin's own family-illness news and visit plans.

b2-015.reason: Reply para 3 agrees with Lyell's paras 5-6 view that most species are immutable and only a few become modified.

b2-016.reason: Reply para 2 opens on being unable to hear from his son about the farm before the sale (incoming paras 3-5), not just the Alford visit of para 6.

b2-017.reason: Reply paras 2-3 question whether style curvature is mere growth, responding to Hooker's paras 6-7 force-of-growth explanation.

b2-018.reason: Reply para 2 enjoying Owen's 'good setting down' reacts to Falconer's para 1 account of Huxley at Oxford.

b2-022.reason: Reply para 3 on hound versus human gestation and multiple origins answers Lyell's paras 2-3.

b2-023.reason: Reply paras 1, 5-7 entrust the Anwick purchase and payment arrangements to Higgins, answering his paras 1-5 on valuation, auction and deposit.

b2-024.reason: Reply paras 2-4 and 7 on Owen's spite and Sedgwick's Phil. Soc. attack respond to Henslow's paras 2-4 about Owen and Sedgwick.

b2-026.reason: Reply para 2 declines the 16 May Geological Society meeting of Lyell's para 3, giving Etty's fever as the reason.

b2-027.reason: Reply para 2 concedes the danger of admitting a Galapagos-continent connection that Lyell raised in para 3.

b2-028.reason: Reply para 1 thanks Henslow for the Elodea observations of para 1 and mentions seeking further information.

b2-029.reason: Reply para 9 opens 'I have said what I can in defence', dangling without the prior answers, and adds unprompted Dogs manuscript news.

b2-030.reason: Reply para 4 answers a quoted phrase 'extinguished in a given time' that appears nowhere in Lyell's para 7 or elsewhere in the letter.

b2-031.reason: Reply para 4 adds the pig story and Wyman's striped horses from Gray's July 10 note, absent from the diœcio-dimorphous paragraph given.

b2-032.reason: Reply para 1 defends the statement about hive bees and red clover that Hardy's para 1 disputes.

b2-033.reason: Reply para 6 on the impertinence of Royalty asking Hooker to lecture answers Hooker's para 5 royal-lecture news and secrecy request.

b2-034.reason: Reply para 1 thanks Hooker for settling Leschenaultia stigma (paras 1-4) and asks about Brown's remarks (para 5).

b2-036.reason: Reply para 6 addresses New Zealand bats not becoming non-volant, raised in Lyell's paras 6-7.

b2-037.reason: Only 'I blundered about the Ant-insect' answers para 10; the extended praise of Murray's generosity to an antagonist responds to his concessions in paras 1-3.

b2-039.reason: Reply para 6 is only the valediction 'Farewell my kind friend | Yours most truly | C. Darwin'.

b2-041.reason: Reply para 1 thanks Murray and clarifies prepotency and 'marrying hermaphrodite opposites', both from Murray's paras 1-2.

b2-042.reason: Reply para 3 is only the valediction 'My good old friend | Yours most truly | C. Darwin'.

b2-043.reason: Reply para 7 on Etty's fever returning answers Hooker's para 1 relief at Etty's good news and question about change of air.

b2-045.reason: Reply para 3 explains why atolls would not retain mammals, answering Lyell's para 3 atoll objection.

b2-046.reason: Reply para 1 reacts to Huxley's Von Baer news (paras 1-3) and asks that Von Baer send anything he publishes.

b2-047.reason: Reply para 4 on no reptile becoming a mammal and a single mammalian progenitor answers Lyell's paras 4-5.

b2-048.reason: Reply para 2 thanks Murray for the 'abominable animal' note mentioned in his para 3.

b2-049.reason: Reply para 1 opens on not showing Lyell's letter to Hooker, and para 8 attacks a 'distinct successive types' quote; neither appears in paras 1-4, 10.

b2-050.reason: Reply para 4 thanks Hooker for the Leschenaultia and Scævola stigma homologies in his paras 2-3.

b2-052.reason: Reply para 7 on the polar bear case and no incipient shore-feeding seals answers Lyell's para 7 seal objection.

b2-054.reason: Reply para 5 on the antiquity of islands and the Canary miocene shells responds to Lyell's paras 4, 6-7.

b3-001.reason: Reply para 4 thanks Hooker for the Elatine note (incoming para 5); the Goodenia and Croker thanks are passing acknowledgement.

b3-002.reason: Answer reports Darwin's own exchange with Symonds on the geological record; it does not respond to Lyell's remark that Asa Gray fears that argument.

b3-004.reason: Reply para 9 answers Falconer's Apteryx clavicle point and the sternal keel remark in incoming paras 7-8.

b3-006.reason: Reply paras 13 and 15 respond to Lyell's 'Variation & Nat. Selection' terminology and his objection that selection does too much work (para 11).

b3-007.reason: Reply para 5 acknowledges Lyell's thanks for the reminder about New Guinea marsupials in incoming para 11.

b3-008.reason: Reply paras 2, 3, 11 give method advice (glass support, drop size, disc inflection) on the experiments described in incoming paras 3-7.

b3-009.reason: Reply paras 7-8 answer Lyell's claim in para 5 that only a few species vary; paras 1-2 set the same island context.

b3-010.reason: Reply para 8 answers paras 6 and 8, but para 9 adds a separate topic, the Dingo's antiquity and man's antiquity, which the question never raises.

b3-012.reason: Reply para 12 endorses the self-supplied answer and the simile of man keeping down new men in incoming para 13.

b3-013.reason: Reply para 5 takes up the tucutucu blindness, inherited mutilations and embryonic eye arrest raised in incoming para 7.

b3-014.reason: Reply para 1 thanks Hooker for the extracts and discusses Dionaea feeding and sensitivity, matching incoming paras 1-3.

b3-016.reason: Reply para 4 responds to 'alter one's speculations' (para 8) and the rank of birds versus monotremes (para 10).

b3-017.reason: Reply para 6 directly answers the question in para 3 about turtles becoming land tortoises on islands.

b3-019.reason: Reply para 10 responds to the suggestion in para 9 about natural root-grafting of fir stumps.

b3-021.reason: Reply para 6 answers Lyell's point on the capacity to vary and his Red Indian case in incoming paras 1-2.

b3-022.reason: Reply paras 4 and 8 respond to the rate and form of incurving of the unnamed Australian Drosera (incoming para 4).

b3-023.reason: Reply para 7 answers the point in para 13 that more isolated human races existed in earlier times.

b3-025.reason: Reply para 4 responds to the Nata cattle and bull-dog cod analogy in incoming paras 2-3.

b3-035.reason: Reply para 3 answers para 2's point about why pigeons were not crossed with other species.

b3-037.reason: Reply para 8 answers Falconer's objection about the chronology of elephants and mastodons in para 14.
